legal.summary: Bar & Bench published an analysis on managing Intellectual Property (IP) ownership structures within Global Capability Centres (GCCs) operating in India. The piece highlights essential legal frameworks for multinational parent entities, focusing on robust IP assignment drafting, clear work-for-hire clauses for employees and third-party vendors, cross-border transfer pricing (TP) alignment, and proactive IP protection strategies under Indian law.
legal.contextNote: Indian GCCs frequently face IP ownership leakages and transfer pricing disputes. Under Section 17(c) and Section 19 of the Copyright Act, 1957, and Section 68 of the Patents Act, 1970, IP assignment must be in writing and specifically state present assignment rather than a future promise to assign. On the tax side, Indian Revenue authorities scrutinize DEMPE (Development, Enhancement, Maintenance, Protection, Exploitation) functions under Section 92 of the Income Tax Act, 1961. (1) In-house counsel must audit existing employment and vendor contracts to replace 'agrees to assign' language with explicit 'hereby assigns' present assignments covering future IP. (2) Counsel must verify that local TP documentation accurately reflects whether the GCC acts as a low-risk contract R&D service provider or a co-owner performing DEMPE functions to avoid heavy tax adjustments. (3) Ensure all patent applications generated at Indian GCCs secure appropriate foreign filing permissions under Section 39 of the Patents Act before filing overseas.
